data.exact_reserve_text: A favourable run off deviation (prior accident year release) of $8.4m (2014: favourable run off deviation of $169.1m) was experienced during the year in respect of various lines of business. Most significantly releases within aviation ($7.2m), marine ($5.4m), liability ($10.7m) where offset by increases in reinsurance ($20.2m). This is mainly due to a reduction in the ultimate loss estimates.
data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a gross prior year reserve release of $28.6 million in 2015, primarily driven by favourable run-off deviation and a reduction in ultimate loss estimates. This gross release was partially offset by a reinsurance release of $20.2 million, resulting in a net prior year release of $8.4 million. Specific lines of business contributing to the net releases included aviation ($7.2 million), marine ($5.4 million), and liability ($10.7 million). The 2013 year of account was closed at the end of 2015 with a return equal to 7.1% of capacity, indicating favourable development for that year. The syndicate also incurred several large losses in the current year, including Tianjin and UK Flooding.
raw_causal_phrases: favourable run off deviation (prior accident year release)
reduction in the ultimate loss estimates
increase in the level of attritional losses
several large losses including Tianjin and UK Flooding
unexpected losses arising from fluctuations in the timing, frequency and severity of claims compared to expectations
changes in the mix of business
challenging market conditions affecting gross written premiums particularly in the Treaty Reinsurance and Energy books
2014 benefited from very low levels of attritional losses and claims for natural catastrophes
The greatest likelihood of significant losses to the syndicate arises from catastrophe events, such as flood damage, windstorm or earthquake

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: The prior year development amount for individual lines of business (aviation, marine, liability) are stated as net releases in the report. The gross prior year development was calculated from the stated net release and reinsurance movement. The claims development triangle is distorted by a Reinsurance to Close (RITC) transaction for 2013 and prior years of account into 2014, making it unreliable for direct prior year development calculation.
